01.event: Rabbi Yohanan objects to Rabbi Elazar's teaching that the unlearned will not be resurrected; Rabbi Elazar defends it from another verse
01.turn: Rabbi Elazar sees that Rabbi Yohanan is grieved
01.outcome: Rabbi Elazar tells him he has found a remedy for the unlearned in the Torah
01.summary: Rabbi Yohanan rebukes Rabbi Elazar for saying the unlearned will not be resurrected, and Rabbi Elazar defends his reading from another verse. Seeing Rabbi Yohanan grieved, Rabbi Elazar tells him he has found a remedy for them in the Torah.
01.missing: Any event beyond speech other than Rabbi Yohanan's grief; the remedy itself is only completed in the context segment
01.reason: Almost entirely an exegetical dialogue, but there is conflict and an emotional reaction (grief) that prompts a change in Rabbi Elazar's stance; mainly speech with some event and change is borderline.

02.event: Seeing priests demean widows, the court raised widows' ketubah to two hundred
02.turn: Grooms then avoided priestly widows in favor of Israelite virgins
02.outcome: The court restored the original amount
02.summary: The priestly court saw that widows were being demeaned and raised their marriage contract. When men then shunned the widows, the court reversed the ordinance.
02.missing: Named individuals or a single concrete incident; it is a history of an institution's ordinances given to resolve a legal contradiction
02.reason: There are real narrated actions with causality and change, but it is an anonymous institutional history of a legal enactment cited to reconcile sources rather than an incident involving persons; it sits between story and not, so borderline.

03.missing: Any event beyond a chance meeting framing a question and answer
03.reason: A setting (Rav Aha found Rav Ashi's students) followed by a question and answer is not a story, as with Shabbat 147a.

04.missing: The content of the incident; only that a case occurred and was brought from Rav Hisda to Rav Huna and resolved from a mishnah
04.reason: An unspecified incident brought before rabbis and resolved by a source; coming before the court is the only event, and the bulk is legal argument.

05.event: His daughter was married to his brother Abba, who died childless
05.turn: Rabban Gamliel took his daughter's rival wife in levirate marriage
05.outcome: The Gemara uses it as a precedent and debates it
05.summary: Rabban Gamliel's daughter was married to his brother Abba, who died childless. Rabban Gamliel then married her co-wife in levirate marriage, which the Gemara cites and questions as a legal precedent.
05.missing: Any response, conflict or consequence beyond the levirate marriage; it is cited as evidence and immediately argued over
05.reason: Something happens to someone (a death) and a person responds with an action (levirate marriage), but it is a compressed precedent followed by legal discussion with little development; between not and borderline, so borderline.

06.missing: Any event beyond Mar Zutra's habitual practice and an objection
06.reason: This is the Mar Zutra halitza-document passage Jeff ruled a bare report of practice with no continuation.

07.event: Me'oret made her slave perform three of the dangerous actions
07.summary: A woman named Me'oret had her slave do three of the listed actions, and he died. The Gemara cites this as a challenge and explains he was already weak.
07.missing: Context, motive, any detail of the incident; it is only alluded to as evidence
07.reason: There are two events with causality (the actions, the death), but the incident is only alluded to inside a legal give-and-take; an alluded incident is borderline.

08.missing: Any event beyond an encounter framing a question and an exegetical answer
08.reason: Rabbi Yosei meets Elijah and asks a question that Elijah answers; a setting plus question and answer is not a story.

09.missing: Any narrated action or change besides a query sent to Rabba and his ruling
09.reason: A document's case is sent to a rabbi and he rules; a case before a rabbi and his ruling, with nothing else happening, is not a story.

10.event: He wished to give away his many movables as a gift but was told it could only be done via land
10.turn: He acquired a small rocky plot near Jerusalem and assigned the movables along with portions of it
10.outcome: He died, and the Sages carried out his instructions
10.summary: A wealthy Madonite in Jerusalem wanted to give away his movable property but was told it could only be transferred by means of land. He bought a plot near Jerusalem and gave portions of it with sheep and barrels to recipients. He died, and the Sages fulfilled his words.
10.reason: An actual incident (maaseh) with several actions, a problem, a response and an outcome, followed by the Sages' implementing act; that meets the 'at least two actions and a change' standard.

11.actor: Rava and Rav Mari bar Rahel
11.event: Rava declared Rav Mari bar Rahel, son of a gentile father, fit
11.outcome: Rava appointed him an official of Babylonia
11.summary: Rava ruled that Rav Mari bar Rahel was of fit lineage and appointed him as one of the officials of Babylonia, which the Gemara justifies exegetically.
11.missing: Any incident, response or development beyond the ruling and appointment
11.reason: Largely a report of a ruling cited as halakha, but the appointment is an act that changes someone's status; sitting between a bare report and a minimal event, it is borderline.

12.missing: Anything beyond a historical note that the returning exiles camped at a well and were permitted to draw from it by inherited custom
12.reason: A baraita explaining the source of a legal permission, with a single event (encamping) followed by a ruling and no change; not a story.

13.event: Rava publicly taught a ruling and Rav Pappa challenged it from a baraita
13.turn: Rava appointed an amora and publicly retracted
13.outcome: He announced that his earlier statement was a mistake and gave the correct teaching
13.summary: After Rav Pappa challenged his ruling, Rava set up an amora and publicly declared that his previous teaching had been his own error, teaching the correct law instead.
13.missing: Any event beyond teaching and retracting, which are speech acts
13.reason: Retraction and teaching are speech; the challenge is ordinary scholarly back-and-forth, not conflict in the R-C2 sense, so there is no story.

14.missing: Any event beyond a boast and an exegetical question and answer
14.reason: Abaye invites questions and a sage challenges his exegesis, which he answers with a baraita; standard rabbinic dialogue without conflict or event is not a story.

15.missing: Any event beyond a visit, an observation and a ruling
15.reason: Rav Avya happens to visit and rules on a bolt he sees; a setting that frames a ruling is not a story.

16.actor: Residents of a shepherds' village and Rav Yehuda
16.event: A sea inlet breached a courtyard wall
16.turn: The case came before Rav Yehuda
16.summary: Rav Yosef recalls that a sea inlet broke into a courtyard in a shepherds' village; the case came before Rav Yehuda, who required only a single board.
16.missing: Any further action or change after the ruling
16.reason: One event followed by a ruling, with nothing changing afterward, is not a story per Jeff's 2026-10-25 ruling.

17.missing: Any event beyond silence, a suggested answer and praise
17.reason: Rav Dimi falls silent, Abaye offers an answer, and Rav Dimi praises him; this is ordinary study-hall dialogue without conflict.

18.missing: Any one-time event or consequence; it reports Rav Hisda's standing practice
18.reason: A report of what Rav Hisda habitually did (refusing to rule in his teacher's lifetime), cited as evidence, with nothing following.

19.event: The Rabbis urged him to marry and have children
19.turn: He deflected, saying he would have had children from his first wife
19.outcome: The Gemara explains he had become impotent from Rav Huna's long discourses
19.summary: The Rabbis told Rabbi Abba bar Zavda to marry and have children, and he put them off by saying that if he had merited he would have had them from his first wife. The Gemara explains the real reason: he had been made infertile by sitting through Rav Huna's lengthy lectures.
19.missing: A narrated outcome or further action; the impotence is explained rather than narrated
19.reason: Mainly an exchange of speech, but a real event (his becoming infertile from Rav Huna's discourse) is mentioned with causality; mainly speech with an event is borderline.

20.event: Rav Yehuda, nearly blind, struggled to read and sign documents
20.turn: Ulla told him it was unnecessary, citing Rabbi Elazar and Rav Nahman who had documents read to them
20.summary: Rav Yehuda, whose eyesight was failing, took great pains to read documents before signing. Ulla told him he need not, since great authorities had scribes read documents to them before signing.
20.missing: Whether Rav Yehuda changed his practice; any outcome
20.reason: There is a real situation (his distress over failing sight) and a response, but it is mainly advice with no narrated change; between a bare report and a minimal story, so borderline.
